status: CORRECTED AND PROVEN — BUT C11 NOT RESUMED: ONE HIGH REMAINS OPEN ELSEWHERE
recordedBy: Claude (implementer). Nothing here claims owner provenance.
authority: Gatekeeper decision PROJECTOS — C11-W2-F1 DELEGATION AUTHORITY CORRECTION1A: source correction authorised for C11-W2-F1 only; fix the authority invariant rather than granting phase-closure to fit a broken vocabulary.

theDefect.summary: The gatekeeper's decider was read from a delegation record that only the plan-approval path ever validated.
theDefect.detail: committedDelegatedDecider accepted the committed record on two facts: programmeScope matched, and delegatedTo was a non-empty string. Schema, owner provenance, delegated scope and the implementer exclusion were checked by checkClosureDelegationRecord — but only while a plan was being approved. The same bytes could therefore be REJECTED by the approval path and simultaneously ACCEPTED as the authority behind every review decision, and whether a record was judged at all depended on the order of events: commit the delegation after plan approval and the validating path never saw it.
theDefect.discoveredBy: The C11 degraded-mode witness, whose owner-approved delegation carried a scope the vocabulary did not have.

testsChanged: projectos/agent/test/planApproval.test.ts (2 tests added, 1 expectation corrected to the pruning decision)

narrowCapability.addedTo: the EXISTING delegation vocabulary in core, as DELEGABLE_SCOPES = CLOSURE_SCOPES + this one
narrowCapability.notASecondSystem: No parallel delegation architecture was created. The record, the file, the validator and the commit gate are all the ones that already existed.
narrowCapability.typeSeparation: It is deliberately not a ClosureScope, so it cannot be passed as ClosureAuthorityInput.scope at all. The vocabulary duplication between core and planApproval was also removed — planApproval had its own copy of CLOSURE_SCOPES, and two lists that must agree but are edited separately is how a scope becomes legal at one boundary and refused at another.

theCorrection.consumptionSideValidation: resolveDelegatedDecider now calls the same checkClosureDelegationRecord the approval path calls, with requiredScope. No second or weaker validator was written; the owner it is judged against comes from resolveRecordedOwner, extracted from approvePlan and shared.
theCorrection.closureLeakageClosedSeparately: materialisePlan no longer writes a delegation carrying no closure scope into governance.closureDelegation, and no longer lets it set closureAuthority. Without this, approving a plan would have handed closure authority to a review-only delegate as a side effect. authoriseClosure would still have refused the close; this stops the claim being made.
theCorrection.pruning: A record carrying both a review scope and a closure scope is materialised with only the closure half. The plan schema's closureDelegation.delegatedScope enum is closure-only by definition — 'Closure only. Protected actions are not delegable through this field.' Copying the review scope through made the plan fail its own schema; widening the schema would have put a capability in a governed field nothing reads it from.
theCorrection.failClosedNotCrash: Judging the record now needs the governance engine, which this function never needed before. A caller reaching it early gets a refusal carrying the real error text rather than an unhandled throw.

additionalFindingsFixedInTheSameCorrecti.severity: CRITICAL (as rated by the ECC security review of the first draft of this fix)
additionalFindingsFixedInTheSameCorrecti.title: The anchor a delegation was judged against was itself forgeable
additionalFindingsFixedInTheSameCorrecti.detail: checkClosureDelegationRecord compares the record to this project's id and recorded owner. Those were read from the WORKING TREE. So anything that can write a file could point planMemory.planPath at a plan naming an owner of its choosing, commit one internally consistent delegation naming that same owner, and be resolved as the decider — every check passing because the expectations had been moved to meet the record. Validating against a forgeable anchor is not validating.
additionalFindingsFixedInTheSameCorrecti.fix: resolveRecordedOwner gained an explicit planTrust mode. Plan approval keeps 'working-tree', unchanged — it is one owner-attended act whose output is then committed. The consumption boundary passes 'committed' and reads project-config.json from HEAD as well: it runs unattended and repeatedly, with no gate of its own, so it takes only bytes that passed one.
additionalFindingsFixedInTheSameCorrecti.provenBy: Tests H, H2, H3, H4 — forging the owner and the project id in the working copy, and removing each anchor from HEAD.

additionalFindingsFixedInTheSameCorrecti.title: A retired programme's delegation could be revived by an unreviewed edit
additionalFindingsFixedInTheSameCorrecti.detail: programmeId came from the uncommitted gatekeeper.json, and a delegation record carries no expiry — it stops applying only because the programme moved on. Re-pointing the programme in the working copy alone would therefore decide which committed delegation applies.
additionalFindingsFixedInTheSameCorrecti.fix: loadGatekeeperConfig reads the committed gatekeeper.json; a working copy that disagrees, or a committed file declaring no programme, is refused by name. The delegation is resolved only when they agree.

gatekeeperTestList.I trueOrderIndependence: in ONE project's timeline: nothing committed, then an approval-boundary judgment, then the bad record committed AFTERWARDS — refused for exactly the same reasons a fresh judgment gives
gatekeeperTestList.C narrowReviewDelegation: resolves the decider; phase closure and programme closure both refused with DELEGATION_SCOPE_MISMATCH

reProvenAgainstTheWitness.result: The owner-approved witness delegation — scope gatekeeper-review-decisions, bytes unchanged — resolves to 'ChatGPT' under the fully corrected semantics, including the committed-anchor requirement. The same query for programme projectos-autonomous-self-hosting is refused as scoped elsewhere. No legitimate invariant unrelated to the scope vocabulary refuses it.

openHigh.title: approvePlan's owner and project-identity anchors remain working-tree-sourced
openHigh.detail: resolveRecordedOwner defaults to planTrust 'working-tree' and approvePlan uses that default; proposal.projectId is likewise derived from the working-tree project-config.json via buildProposal. This is the same forgeable-anchor pattern that was just closed at the gatekeeper boundary, on the module's most consequential function — the only route by which a record carrying PLAN READY comes into existence. Because the forged anchor file is never part of the commit being reviewed, it evades the 'a forged one is a visible diff' guarantee the module's threat model rests on.
openHigh.whyNotFixedHere: The source correction was authorised for C11-W2-F1 only, and the scope freeze forbids fixing unrelated findings and optional hardening. Changing how plan approval establishes the owner is a governance decision with real consequences — it would make a project whose active plan is uncommitted unable to approve a successor — and that is the owner's and the gatekeeper's call, not the implementer's.
openHigh.consequence: The stated precondition for resuming C11 is CRITICAL = 0 and HIGH = 0. It is not met. C11 was NOT resumed.

openLow: The catch in resolveDelegatedDecider is broader than the anticipated engine-not-installed case, so a genuine internal bug would present as an ordinary refusal rather than a loud failure. It fails closed either way and surfaces the real error text.
requiredScope was typed as plain string; it is now typed to the DelegableScope vocabulary.
eccReview.reviewCaveat: The security re-review read the code while the last cosmetic cleanups were being applied. It re-verified against a stable snapshot, but the final two changes after it finished — typing requiredScope, and the earlier LOW cleanups — were not in front of it. Neither changes any security semantics.

c17Relationship: C17 was not reopened and its historical evidence was not rewritten. C11-W2-F1 was discovered after C17 closure and is recorded here as a new post-closure HIGH against the current authority boundary, now corrected. The post-correction review demonstrates CRITICAL = 0 for the corrected boundary; the one remaining HIGH is the separate pre-existing finding above.
recommendation: READY IN SUBSTANCE, BLOCKED BY RULE. C11-W2-F1 is corrected, proven and mutation-tested, and the witness delegation is valid under the corrected semantics with its owner-approved bytes untouched. C11 was not resumed because the post-fix review leaves one HIGH open — C11-W2-F5, pre-existing and out of the authorised scope. The gatekeeper should rule: correct C11-W2-F5 under fresh authority before resuming, or accept it as pre-existing and separately scheduled and let C11 proceed. The implementer should not make that call.
